results.summary_before: Rule 30 Engine iterates a 56-bit Rule 30 cellular automaton starting from an 8-bit initial value supplied on the input bus. Each iteration is transmitted over an 8N1 UART at 115,200 baud on output pin uo[4], with zero boundary conditions around the 56-bit field. The only external hardware needed is a UART receiver to capture the serial output. The documentation is brief and does not include silicon test results or details about the internal implementation.

results.summary_before: This design implements an anomaly detection system using an isolation tree algorithm, intended for integration into SoCs with AI accelerators. It consists of an input buffer that collects sensor data bit-by-bit, and a state machine that processes the data to detect anomalies based on a predefined byte pattern. The design is currently simplistic, checking against a set pattern, but is intended to be expanded to more complex algorithms. It requires a binary output sensor as external hardware and is designed for real-time anomaly detection in embedded applications.

results.summary_before: This is a simple TTL pulse generator that produces one of sixteen pre-programmed pulse sequences selected by a 4-bit input. The selected sequence appears on a single TTL output pin, and the design is intended to be tested by setting the sequence select pins and observing the output. No external hardware is required beyond the chip itself, though the documentation does not describe the sequences or their timing. The documentation is very thin, providing only the basic function and pin usage.
